post.caption:
The potato produced more calories per acre than any grain, grew on poorer soil, and could not be burned by a passing army because the crop was underground. Europe's population climbed steeply within a century of adoption. Ireland went furthest, and depended not just on potatoes but largely on one variety, so when blight arrived that beat that variety it beat the whole food supply. A million died and a million left.
